def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Find the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a Max-Heap approach.
    The average and worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is O(n + k log n).
    """
    import heapq
    
    if k < 1 or k > len(nums):
        raise ValueError("k is out of bounds of the list.")
    
    # Create a max-heap by inverting the values (using min-heap implementation)
    max_heap = [-num for num in nums]
    heapq.heapify(max_heap)
    
    # Extract the maximum k times
    largest = None
    for _ in range(k):
        largest = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)
    
    return largest

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Find the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Heap Select algorithm.
    The average time complexity of this algorithm is O(n + k log k) and the worst-case time complexity is O(n log k).
    """
    import heapq
    
    if k < 1 or k > len(nums):
        raise ValueError("k is out of bounds of the list.")
    
    # Create a min-heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)
    
    # Iterate over the rest of the elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest element from the heap
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Push the current number onto the heap
    
    return min_heap[0]
